text:
This first round tests the cleanest hypothesis from the generating rule.

**Why the irrelevant features can go:** the label depends only on five properties: impurity_ratio, grain_spread, lattice_density, anneal_temp and cooling_rate. The other five play no part. Those are facet_count, luminance, hydration, edge_curvature and isotope_shift, which are features 5–9, 15–19 and 25–29. All 15 of those columns are pure noise with respect to the label.

**Why this should help:** the network fits training data almost perfectly (train loss 0.074) but does much worse on validation (0.288). That gap suggests it has partly fitted noise in those columns. They are z-scored with mean around 0, so zeroing their input weights mostly removes random variation from the hidden layer rather than shifting it.

**The edit:** set all W1 rows for those 15 features to zero, which is 240 weights. Nothing else changes. The relevant features, including the noisier _peak and _spread versions, are left alone for now.

**Fallback:** if validation gets worse, the network was using those columns to offset errors elsewhere. In that case I'll revert and try a partial version, such as zeroing only the irrelevant _spread rows or shrinking the rows by half instead of zeroing them.
